scenes.title: Add Unit Alerts and understand the empty state

captions.text: Unit Alerts helps a coordination team find units that have remained in a timed
status longer than the department expects.
In Big Board, use the plus icon and choose Unit Alerts from Add Widget.
Scroll to the new panel.
This department initially shows No status timers configured.
That message describes the missing timer configuration; it does not establish
that every unit has reported promptly.
The thresholds are department settings managed in the Core website.
In Core, open Department Settings, choose Operations, then
Mapping and BigBoard Settings.
Scroll to Unit Status Timers.
The table separates Status, Warn after in minutes, and Alert after in minutes.
Each displayed status has its own row, including Dispatched,
Responding, En Route and On Scene.
Initially, both columns are zero throughout this training table.
The helper text explains that leaving both at zero times nothing.
Choose values that fit your department's reporting process.
For this software exercise, enter two under Warn after and four under
Alert after on the Responding row.
Leave the other rows unchanged.
These are demonstration values, not a recommended response standard.
The two columns allow the department to distinguish a warning interval from a
later alert interval for the same status.
Review the row label and both minute values before saving, so the timer applies
to the intended operational meaning.

scenes.title: Require a reason and read back the saved settings

captions.text: Below the table, set Reason when acknowledging to Required
for warnings and alerts.
The help explains that this policy applies when acknowledging
or muting a status timer alert.
Select Save.
Reload Mapping and BigBoard Settings and return to the table:
Responding still shows two and four.
Scroll down again and verify the required-reason selection.
Reading back both controls checks the saved configuration before you
examine its effect in Big Board.

scenes.title: Inspect the overdue unit on the refreshed board

captions.text: Reload Big Board.
Unit Alerts now shows Squad Three, its Responding state, Firehouse Fifty One
and the elapsed time in that state.
This fictional record is already more than one hundred eighty hours
old, far beyond the four-minute alert threshold, so it appears red immediately.
The elapsed value helps identify a status report needing review.
It does not explain why the report is old.
Use the unit's normal reporting and coordination process to investigate.

scenes.title: Acknowledge with a reason and inspect the saved result
visual_required_labels: A reason is required before this alert can be acknowledged or muted.
TRAINING ONLY - Timer review practice; verify the unit state with the exercise coordinator.

captions.text: Select the Squad Three row to open Unit status alert.
With Reason empty, the sheet explains the requirement and
disables Acknowledge and Mute.
Enter the clearly labeled training reason, then select Acknowledge.
Reopen the row.
The saved section now says Seen by Wallace Boden and retains the exercise note.
Acknowledging records that review; the unit still has its Responding state.
The sheet also offers Clear acknowledgement for removing
the saved acknowledgement.

scenes.title: Give the panel enough space for its note
visual_required_labels: Seen by Wallace Boden: TRAINING ONLY - Timer review practice; verify the unit state with the exercise coordinator.

captions.text: If the small alert panel clips the saved note, open the gear
settings and select Unit Alerts.
Under Widget Size, this example uses width four and height three grid units.
Select Save and return to the panel.
The wider, taller result shows the unit, state, reviewer and
complete training note together.
required_labels: Seen by Wallace Boden: TRAINING ONLY - Timer review practice; verify the unit state with the exercise coordinator.

captions.text: Reopening these settings after a later reload still shows four by three.
Check the rendered result as well as the values in the editing form.

scenes.title: Save and inspect a fifteen-minute training mute
visual_required_labels: TRAINING ONLY - Practice a fifteen-minute mute; no operational response is being suppressed.
Seen by Wallace Boden: TRAINING ONLY - Practice a fifteen-minute mute; no operational response is being suppressed.

captions.text: Open the same alert again.
Under Mute for, select fifteen minutes.
Replace the reason with the note describing this fictional
mute exercise, then choose Mute.
The panel now has a collapsed Muted, one, section.
Expand it to see Squad Three and the saved mute reason.
required_labels: Seen by Wallace Boden: TRAINING ONLY - Practice a fifteen-minute mute; no operational response is being suppressed.

captions.text: The unit still says Responding.
Moving an alert into this section changes how the timer alert is presented; it does
not resolve the underlying unit state.

scenes.title: Verify persistence and clear the saved mute
visual_required_labels: TRAINING ONLY - Practice a fifteen-minute mute; no operational response is being suppressed.

captions.text: Reload Big Board, expand Muted, one, and reopen Squad Three.
The sheet retains the reviewer and reason and displays a Muted until time.
This checks that the saved mute survived a reload.
For this exercise, choose Clear acknowledgement.
The unit returns to the active red alert panel, because its
unchanged Responding record is still beyond the configured threshold.
The timer, saved acknowledgement or mute, and underlying unit status
are separate things to verify.

scenes.title: Apply the review process across departments

captions.text: A security control room can use status timers to review a delayed patrol update.
Search-and-rescue coordinators can follow a team's reporting interval.
Community paramedicine and mental health response teams, wildland
contractors, industrial response teams, and fire and E M S departments can
apply the same review process with appropriate statuses and thresholds.
Configure the timer, inspect the actual unit and elapsed time,
document the review, and verify the saved result using fictional
data before adopting the process.

context_notes: All original source JPEGs were personally viewed and the complete generated narration was approved by User.
Every original speech cue is mapped in full; the exact gear icon has additional actual browser DOM control evidence.
Core instruction scenes retain Core identity, with an explicit configuration-source declaration; all client operational screens retain BigBoard identity.
Only actual saved/reopened results are described. Unsupported font16 attempts and unexecuted automatic expiry/escalation are excluded.
